venue.name: Beacon Hill Children's Farm
venue.description: Beacon Hill Children's Farm is a small family-run farm in the middle of Beacon Hill Park in Victoria, home to more than a hundred farm animals and open to the public seasonally. It has been family run and operated since June 1985 and is supported by staff and volunteers. Admission is by donation, and the farm's best-known features are its goat petting area and the twice-daily goat stampede.

facility_notes.washrooms: There are no public washrooms inside the farm. The closest washroom is near the playground in the park, about a 3 minute walk from the farm. Handwashing stations with soap and water are near the entrance and the goat petting area.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: All of the paths inside the farm are gravel, with no steep inclines and no stairs. The site answers the accessibility question with this description rather than a yes or no.
facility_notes.bus_parking: There is a parking lot directly outside the farm, along Circle Drive. The site does not say whether a coach can park or set down there.
facility_notes.rain_backup: The farm's scheduled programs are weather permitting and do not run in rain or strong wind. No indoor alternative is mentioned.

venue.nearby_park: The farm sits in the middle of Beacon Hill Park. The nearest public washroom is by the playground, about a 3-minute walk.
restrictions: Please only come to visit the farm if everyone in your group feels healthy.
Remember to wash your hands before and after visiting with the animals.
Adult supervisors should monitor young children to ensure that they do not put their fingers or any objects in their mouth while in animal areas.
There is a maximum capacity for the goat petting area on busy days; without a booking a group may not be able to enter it.
venue.hours_notes: The site does not publish daily opening hours; its Contact & Hours page returns a 404. It does state daily goat stampedes at 10:10 am and 5:10 pm, lunchtime animal feedings between 11:30 am and 12:30 pm, and earliest group booking times of 10:30 am in spring and fall and 11:00 am in July and August.
venue.seasonal_notes: The farm runs a public season and an off season, and the site opens with 'Welcome back for the 2026 season!'. The published Animal Talks schedule covers August 4 to September 1. The months the farm is open are not stated.
venue.price_year_or_season: 2026 season; suggested donation amounts described as 'this year's'

programs.name: Group visit
programs.description: A booked visit for schools, childcare centres and summer camps. All groups of 10 or more must book at least 48 hours ahead by email; the farm recommends booking in April or May because the calendar fills up in spring. Earliest booking time is 10:30 am in spring and fall and 11:00 am in July and August, and groups are welcome to arrive at 10:10 am to watch the goat stampede before their scheduled entry to the petting area.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the gravel farmyard among more than a hundred animals, go into the goat petting area at a booked time, and can watch the goat stampede at 10:10 am or the pigs, donkeys and alpacas being fed between 11:30 and 12:30.
programs.our_note: Book earlier than you think you need to. The farm says spring fills up and asks for April or May. The thing to plan around is washrooms: there are none inside the farm and the nearest is a three-minute walk, which is a long way with a line of four-year-olds.
programs.practical_summary: No washrooms inside the farm, no indoor shelter if it rains, and gravel paths throughout with no stairs or steep inclines. Handwashing stations are by the entrance and the goat area. Lunch space and coach parking are not addressed anywhere on the site.
programs.extra_fees_note: No admission fee is charged. The farm runs on donations and suggests $7 per adult and $6 per child, adding that any amount a group can give is appreciated.
programs.cancellation_note: A minimum of 24 hours notice is appreciated to cancel or reschedule, so the slot can be offered to another group.
programs.evidence: all groups of 10 or more participants (including schools, childcare centres, and summer camps) must book their visit in advance

programs.name: Farm Friends Storytime
programs.description: A weekly drop-in storytime for young children, held Thursdays from 10:45 to 11:15 am. Each week has a different theme and new stories, followed by meeting the animals and colouring. No registration is required. The farm asks that large groups do not attend, and states that daycares of 10 or fewer children may come.
programs.what_children_do: Sit together for a story on a farm theme, then meet the animals and colour at the farm.
programs.our_note: This is the one offering here built for two- to five-year-olds, and at thirty minutes it is the right length for them. Note the cap: the farm asks for daycare groups of ten or fewer, so a full room may need to split across two Thursdays. It is cancelled outright in rain or strong wind.
programs.practical_summary: Thursdays 10:45 to 11:15, drop-in with no registration, and free beyond the suggested donation. Cancelled in rain or strong wind, and there are no washrooms inside the farm.
programs.extra_fees_note: No fee is stated for the storytime itself. Farm admission is by donation, suggested $7 per adult and $6 per child.
programs.cancellation_note: Weather permitting - no program in the event of rain or strong wind.
programs.evidence: Ages: 2-5 years (younger and older siblings welcome!)

programs.name: Weekly Animal Talks
programs.description: A weekly drop-in talk held Tuesdays at 12:00 pm, featuring a different animal each week. The published schedule ran August 4 (senior animals - donkeys), August 11 (chickens), August 18 (guinea pigs), August 25 (pigs) and September 1 (senior animals - donkeys). No registration is required.
programs.what_children_do: Gather round one kind of animal - donkeys, chickens, guinea pigs or pigs, depending on the week - and hear about it from farm staff.
programs.our_note: A short, free add-on rather than a reason to make the trip on its own, and it lands at noon, which may collide with lunch or naps. Check the schedule before you go: the farm posts it a few weeks at a time and the last date published was September 1.
programs.practical_summary: Tuesdays at noon, drop-in, no registration and no fee. Cancelled in rain or strong wind, and the published schedule only runs to September 1.
programs.extra_fees_note: No fee is stated for the talks. Farm admission is by donation, suggested $7 per adult and $6 per child.
programs.cancellation_note: Weather permitting - no program in the event of rain or strong wind.
programs.evidence: Join us at the farm every Tuesday for our weekly Animal Talks.
